scope: Original papers on training overhead/energy, task-oriented identification, adaptive pilots and known/chosen-plaintext optical recovery. Bounded source check, not exhaustive novelty search.

sources.title: How Much Training Is Needed in Multiple-Antenna Wireless Links?
sources.read_extent: Abstract and original paper Section II; bibliographic data verified in author institution repository.
sources.supported_claim: Optimal training overhead depends on channel, coherence and power constraints. Variable training/data power differs from equal-power training.
sources.project_use: Separate fixed-symbol-energy and fixed-total-energy comparisons; state session/channel coherence.
sources.nontransferable: The MIMO training-length result is not a theorem that three optical parameters require three pilots.
sources.access_note: Author repository temporary signed PDF endpoint inaccessible through browser tool; original-paper university mirror read instead.

sources.title: Training sequence design for MIMO channels: an application-oriented approach
sources.venue: EURASIP Journal on Wireless Communications and Networking 2013, 245
sources.read_extent: Open publisher full text; abstract, Sections 1, 5.3 and 6.
sources.supported_claim: Training can be designed for end-use quality and energy constraints; channel-estimate MSE and equalization performance differ; adaptive pilot choice has feedback overhead.
sources.project_use: Evaluate payload recovery separately from parameter error and charge feedback overhead.
sources.nontransferable: Does not establish payload BER or 99% frame reliability for the Trikey model.

sources.title: Spatially Common Sparsity Based Adaptive Channel Estimation and Feedback for FDD Massive MIMO
sources.read_extent: Author manuscript v3, revised 2023-10-19; abstract, Section III overview and IV-D/IV-G section structure.
sources.supported_claim: Adaptive training overhead and pilot design using spatial sparsity and temporal correlation precede this project.
sources.project_use: Motivates controlled adaptive-training comparison, not a claim of first proposing adaptive pilots.
sources.nontransferable: Wireless sparsity assumptions, thresholds and bounds are not imported into optical simulation. No claim about replication or validation of its theorems.
sources.access_note: Southampton repository returned 403; author arXiv version was accessible.

sources.title: Security analysis of optical encryption
sources.read_extent: Author institution full text; abstract and Sections 1, 3, 4, 5.
sources.supported_claim: Amplitude-encoding DRPE has known/chosen plaintext vulnerabilities; approximate image recovery need not require complete keys. Section 4.1 (PDF page 5, equations 5–7) learns an equivalent linear encryption matrix from input basis vectors and their outputs.
sources.project_use: Separate message recovery from exact parameter estimation.
sources.nontransferable: Original numerical DRPE model is not the current three-layer dual-polarization model; attack rates are not transferred.

sources.title: Known-plaintext attack on optical encryption based on double random phase keys
sources.read_extent: Publisher bibliographic record and abstract only; full text subscription-restricted.
sources.supported_claim: Known plaintext and phase retrieval can recover phase keys in the specified DRPE scheme.
sources.project_use: Public known input/output pairs must be available to both modeled receivers.
sources.nontransferable: No claim of implementing this paper's phase-retrieval algorithm or of a universal pilot-count threshold.

sources.title: Chosen-plaintext attack on lensless double-random phase encoding in the Fresnel domain
sources.read_extent: Publisher bibliographic record and abstract only; full text subscription-restricted.
sources.supported_claim: Impulse-function chosen inputs attack Fresnel L-DRPE; abstract identifies linearity of encryption/decryption as a source of vulnerability.
sources.project_use: Motivates testing an equivalent linear decoder with only actually public training pairs.
sources.nontransferable: A receiver that merely observes protocol pilots must not be given additional chosen-plaintext access.

statistics_sources.title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook, 7.2.4.1 Confidence intervals
statistics_sources.read_extent: Exact binomial and one-sided interval sections
statistics_sources.use: Small failure counts need suitable binomial intervals; distinguish one-sided and two-sided confidence.

statistics_sources.title: SciPy BinomTestResult.proportion_ci, v1.15.0 documentation
statistics_sources.use: Clopper-Pearson implementation definition; actual runtime version must be recorded separately.

derived_statistics_not_paper_results.assumption: Independent Bernoulli sessions, fixed n, all n successes, no multiple-comparison correction
derived_statistics_not_paper_results.warning: Zero failures at n=30 does not confirm 99%; 299 is only the all-success threshold. Freeze n and candidate before confirmation; same-session frames are not independent trials.

novelty_position: A reproducible quantitative protocol specific to the frozen Trikey model can be a project contribution. Any empirical finding must be computed from this study's records. Adaptive pilots and optical known-plaintext recovery are established concepts; no first-ever claim.
source_limitations: Bounded search, not exhaustive prior-art review. Some full text inaccessible; read extent is explicit per source. No source values used as substitute simulation observations.
